segments.text: Computer Science splits into two 100-mark papers: Paper I covers computing fundamentals, programming, object orientation, algorithms and data structures, software engineering, and compilers. Paper II covers computer architecture, networks, operating systems, databases, image processing, and web technologies. Throughout, the most durable exam skill is tracing a mechanism step by step (how a loop actually executes, how a packet actually moves through layers, how a query is actually processed) rather than reciting a definition — definitions are easy to forget under exam pressure, but a mechanism you can re-derive rarely fails you.
